div.div:
A numeric interval of the form (a,b) (a,b] [a,b) or [a,b]. A square bracket means including the boundary, round bracket means excluding the boundary. a and b are decimal numbers.
For strings, the range defines the length of the string. For numbers, the range is the interval in which the number must lie.

div.div: This FDO defines the root profile. Any FDO must be valid against the root profile. The root profile requires three attributes: 0.FDO/Type, 0.FDO/Profile, 0.FDO/Data.These three attributes must be used in any FDO. The root profile can and should be extended by other profiles.

div.div: This FDO profile is the base template to define new attributes. It is extended by five different templates: 0.FDO/AttributeDefSyntax, 0.FDO/AttributeDefComb, 0.FDO/AttributeDefUnion, 0.FDO/AttributeDefProfileRef, and 0.FDO/AttributeDefAttrRef. Each of those templates can be instantiated to define new attributes based on certain validation rules. An attribute that only instantiates 0.FDO/AttributeDef (and none of the extending templates) is validated to be a string.

div.div: An attribute can use several validation mechanisms simultaneously. Which validation mechanism applies depends on the profile(s) used by the attribute definition: 0.FDO/AttributeDefSyntax, 0.FDO/AttributeDefComb, 0.FDO/AttributeDefUnion, 0.FDO/AttributeDefProfileRef, and 0.FDO/AttributeDefAttrRef. If several of these profiles are used by one attribute definition, 0.FDO/ValidationStrategyForCombination determines whether at least one validation mechanism must apply (anyof), or all of them (allof). The default is allof, in which case the attribute can be omitted.
